source.snippet: I manage a single Linux VPS (Ubuntu) and I am currently juggling several separate tools for everyday tasks, which is slowing me down. My daily tasks: SSH into the server to run shell commands. Upload and download files over SFTP or SCP. Manage databases (MySQL and PostgreSQL): running queries, browsing tables, and doing quick backups. Right now I use one client for the terminal, another for file transfer, and a third for the database, and switching between them constantly is tedious.

problem_statement: Developers and freelancers managing Linux VPS servers must switch between three separate tools for SSH terminal access, SFTP file transfer, and database management, creating friction and lost time that a unified GUI client could eliminate.
target_segment: Solo developers, freelancers, and small agencies who self-manage Linux VPS instances and run MySQL/PostgreSQL databases
notes: Single signal but represents a well-known and persistent friction point in the solo-dev/freelancer market. Tool-shopping behavior (actively seeking a product) is a positive indicator. Competing products (TablePlus, Beekeeper Studio, Termius) exist but none fully unify all three workflows. A paid tier for this segment is plausible. Signal strength kept at 2 pending corroboration from additional sources.
